findings.title: Retain a current end-to-end SDLC feedback diagram
findings.trigger: A reader follows the prior Workbench diagram entry point or asks to see the complete SDLC model, as the user did in the latest review request.
findings.intended: Preserve current useful documentation while consolidating duplicate/obsolete representations.
findings.baseline: The diagram README links both editable sources through URL-encoded filenames and four rendered views. The complete lifecycle includes implementation/review, case execution, comparison and distinct return paths for implementation defects, assertion/execution gaps, and intent/evidence gaps. The three-loop concept explicitly relates intent, reality and observed outcomes.
findings.candidate: Both editable sources and all previews/index are deleted. The ledger names ARCHITECTURE.md as the replacement. Its core workflow is linear prose; remaining Mermaid views cover intake/knowledge data flow or static traceability, without the full SDLC feedback/control view.
findings.consequence: The owner loses the visual model they use to understand and discuss the Workbench SDLC; prose and narrower diagrams cannot serve the same complete visual explanation. This is documentation/user value loss, with no runtime outage claim.
findings.owner: Workbench maintainer; named human owner unknown
findings.next_action: Retain/update one stable editable concept and end-to-end lifecycle diagram and link it from a maintained guide. Consolidate duplicate previews as useful; the finding does not require restoring every export.
findings.validation: Compare the maintained view with the three viewpoints and three feedback routes, open it through the current documentation entry point, and inspect its rendered readability.

findings.title: Preserve the supplied-source recovery entry point
findings.trigger: A reviewer opens the retained release-report source-analysis or implementation links from a fresh checkout, which has no tracked core/release-report TypeScript source.
findings.intended: Retain recovery information and source traceability when removing historical reports.
findings.baseline: The preparation guide links the inventory and exact supplied-source archive, states that the source tree is untracked, explains unknown source revision/environment limits, and supplies temporary extraction plus original-path/line-number recovery instructions.
findings.candidate: The archive and inventory remain byte-identical under the owning task, but no tracked Markdown refers to the archive or owning inventory. The retained implementation still links the untracked source at line 19 and states its untracked status at line 65. The replacement case catalog preserves cases, not the source-recovery route.
findings.consequence: Future readers cannot recover original source for retained analysis from the living documentation path; discovering the archive now requires knowing its filename or consulting the migration ledger/Git history. Impact is limited to source review/reproduction usability.
findings.owner: Workbench maintainer; named human owner unknown
findings.next_action: Add a compact source recovery note or evidence index under the owning release-report task, linking archive and inventory and describing safe extraction/original locator reuse.
findings.validation: In a temporary fresh-checkout view without core/release-report, follow a retained source citation through the documented recovery path, extract the archive to a temporary location and resolve the original member/line.
